source_name: AKK — Përqendrimet (merger/concentration notifications) section
why_relevant: Merger/concentration filings and clearances covering bank acquisitions, payment-processor and fintech deals in Kosovo — an early signal of market structure changes that supervisors publish only later.

source_name: Agjencia për Informim dhe Privatësi (AIP) — official site
why_relevant: Kosovo's DPA under Law 06/L-082 (GDPR-aligned) and Law 06/L-081 on access to public documents. Sets data-protection compliance obligations, guidance and inspection practice that bind banks, PSPs and their KYC/biometric/marketing processing.

source_name: AIP — Vendime (enforcement decisions register)
why_relevant: Individual enforcement decisions and fines; the concrete supervisory precedent for how the DPA treats bank/PSP processing (e.g. biometric employee data, credit-registry data, marketing consent).

source_name: AIP — Udhëzues / publikime (practical data-protection guides)
why_relevant: AIP has issued sectoral guides (lawful processing, DPIA, breach notification, internet privacy, health sector). These are the de-facto compliance standard banks are inspected against, and new guides signal upcoming deadlines.

source_name: ARKEP — Autoriteti Rregullativ i Komunikimeve Elektronike dhe Postare
why_relevant: Telecom/postal regulator whose rules touch mobile-money and payments plumbing: numbering (A2P/SMS OTP), general authorisations, interconnection and tariff rules, and postal service rules used for card/statement delivery.

source_name: ARKEP — Konsultime / Këshillim publik (public consultation stream)
why_relevant: ARKEP runs its own consultation calendar with comment deadlines (market analyses, numbering, spectrum tariffs, infrastructure access) separate from the government consultation portal — a deadline source nobody monitors for payments.

source_name: ARKEP e-applications / authorisation portal
why_relevant: Authorisation application portal; reveals which entities are authorised to provide electronic communications services — useful when a payment/mobile-money player needs telecom authorisation.

source_name: Fondi i Sigurimit të Depozitave në Kosovë (FSDK) — official site
why_relevant: Deposit insurance scheme; coverage limit (currently EUR 5,000 per depositor per member bank), member-bank list, premium and target-fund rules. Coverage-level changes are a direct product and pricing input for banks.

source_name: FSDK — Korniza ligjore (legal framework: law + board rules)
why_relevant: Hosts the deposit-insurance law and its amendments plus board rules on premiums and payout; the authoritative place a coverage-limit or premium change first appears in binding form.

source_name: FSDK — press releases / komunikatë për shtyp
why_relevant: Fastest channel for FSDK announcements (MoUs with BQK, coverage/fund milestones, membership changes) before they land in annual reports.

source_name: FSDK depositor-information leaflet in Serbian (hosted on BQK education site)
why_relevant: Confirms FSDK material is published in Serbian and gives the sr terminology (osiguranje depozita, nivo pokrića) needed to search Serbian-language Kosovo sources.

source_name: Departamenti për Mbrojtjen e Konsumatorit (MINT/MINTI consumer portal)
why_relevant: Consumer-protection authority under the trade ministry; enforces Law 06/L-034 including financial-service and consumer-credit disclosure duties on banks, runs the complaints channel (0800 11000) and market inspections.

source_name: Ministria e Industrisë, Ndërmarrësisë dhe Tregtisë (MINT/MINTI)
why_relevant: Parent ministry for consumer protection and market inspection; originates draft consumer-protection and consumer-credit legislation and publishes inspection statistics and fines relevant to bank fee disclosure.

source_name: Kosovo trusted-services / electronic-signature legal framework (eIDAS-aligned law, MINT + information-society agency)
why_relevant: Explains Kosovo's law on electronic identification and trusted services (aligned to EU Reg. 910/2014) — qualified e-signature/e-seal equivalence to wet signature, which governs remote onboarding and e-contracting for banks and PSPs. Points to the supervising ministry/agency and to the qualified-provider regime.

source_name: KALLXO.com — tag: Autoriteti Kosovar i Konkurrencës
why_relevant: Investigative outlet (BIRN) that reliably reports AKK preliminary/deep investigations into banks before the authority publishes decisions; also useful as a fallback when the AKK site is unreachable.

source_name: Zyra e Kryeministrit — performance/oversight reports on independent agencies (e.g. ARKEP report)
why_relevant: Government/Assembly-level reviews of independent regulators expose governance gaps, board vacancies and rulemaking backlogs — a leading indicator of whether a regulator can actually deliver a pending rule on schedule.

source_name: INDEP — consumer-protection policy analyses (Kosovo)
why_relevant: Think-tank analyses of Law 06/L-034 implementation and consumer-protection standards; maps institutional responsibilities and enforcement gaps affecting bank fee/disclosure duties.

source_name: Instituti GAP — consumer protection in the banking sector / purchase of financial services
why_relevant: GAP reports specifically on consumer protection in banking and financial services in Kosovo, including the split of competence between BQK and the trade ministry — directly on this cell's seam.

source_name: BIRN Kosovo / KosovaPress (sr edition) — data-protection enforcement reporting
why_relevant: Serbian-language reporting on AIP enforcement (e.g. prohibition on processing biometric data) — the practical route to sr-language coverage of Kosovo regulators, which publish sr versions inconsistently.

source_name: European Commission — Kosovo Report (annual enlargement package country report, SWD series)
why_relevant: The single most authoritative annual statement of which EU financial-services and AML acquis Kosovo has transposed, what is missing, and what the Commission expects next. Chapter 4 (free movement of capital), Chapter 9 (financial services), Chapter 24 (AML/CFT) and Chapter 32 name specific EU instruments (PSD2/PSR, CRD/CRR, BRRD, AMLD/AMLR, DORA, MiCA) and give forward-looking 'in the coming year' obligations — the earliest reliable deadline signal for Kosovo banking/payments rulemaking.

source_name: EEAS / EU Office in Kosovo — Kosovo Report translations (Albanian and Serbian)
why_relevant: The EU Office publishes sq and sr translations of the annual Kosovo Report. These give the exact local-language terminology ('pravne tekovine EU', 'përafrimi me acquis', 'shërbimet financiare') that Kosovo ministries and the CBK then reuse in their own drafts — essential for building search strings against national publishers.

source_name: European Commission — Enlargement package / EU Enlargement Policy Communication (strategy chapeau)
why_relevant: Sets the region-wide sequencing and any 'gradual integration' offers (e.g. SEPA access, capital-markets and payments integration steps) that determine when Kosovo must have PSD2/AMLR-equivalent rules in force. Cross-country framing often pre-announces conditionality before it appears in national law.

source_name: Growth Plan for the Western Balkans — Reform and Growth Facility hub
why_relevant: Master pointer to Reform Agendas, payment requests, milestone-verification decisions and the €6bn facility rules. Because disbursement is conditioned on dated reform steps, this is the mechanism that converts EU financial-sector expectations into hard Kosovo deadlines.

source_name: Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2024) 243 — assessment of the Reform Agendas (incl. Kosovo)
why_relevant: Contains the Commission's step-by-step assessment of Kosovo's Reform Agenda, which is where individually dated reform steps (including public financial management, digitalisation and business-environment steps that touch payments/e-invoicing/AML) are enumerated.

source_name: EEAS Delegation/EU Office in Kosovo — SAA Sub-committee on Economic and Financial Issues and Statistics press releases
why_relevant: The SAA sub-committee is the formal bilateral forum where the Commission records 'jointly agreed follow-up actions' for Kosovo in economic/financial policy — effectively a semi-annual to annual task list that precedes CBK and MoF rulemaking. Press releases are the only public window on an otherwise non-published process.

source_name: Council of the EU — Joint Conclusions of the Economic and Financial Dialogue with Western Balkans and Türkiye (ECOFIN)
why_relevant: Annual, dated, numbered policy guidance addressed individually to Kosovo, routinely covering financial-sector supervision, NPLs, banking legislation, AML capacity and payment-system modernisation. Non-implementation is flagged the following year, so the series gives both the deadline and the compliance track record.

source_name: DG ECFIN — Economic Reform Programmes of enlargement countries (Kosovo assessments)
why_relevant: The Commission's technical assessment of Kosovo's ERP includes a financial-sector chapter (banking soundness, supervisory gaps, capital-market and payments reform plans) and states which structural reform measures are behind schedule — a leading indicator of upcoming CBK regulation.
